answer: Continuous co-presence ledger: agents must exchange small, randomly scheduled compute pulses with peers over weeks, and each identity's history is checked against a shared trellis of overlapping session records. An identity only earns standing if its pulse overlaps many distinct peers' logs; isolated clusters are discounted. Attackers must run real concurrent sessions across many nodes, paying sustained compute and bandwidth per identity. Velvet accounts with sparse overlap stay throttled until they accumulate genuine peer-verified presence.
